nodes.title: Khare's level-one theorem, with the exact sense of 'arises from'
nodes.statement: Let rho-bar: G_Q -> GL_2(F) be continuous, absolutely irreducible, two-dimensional, odd (det rho-bar(c) = -1), with F a finite field of characteristic p, and suppose rho-bar is unramified outside p, i.e. N(rho-bar) = 1. Then rho-bar arises from S_{k(rho-bar)}(SL_2(Z)) with respect to an embedding iota: Qbar -> Qbar_p. 'Arises from a newform f' means: there is an integral model rho: G_Q -> GL_2(O) of the p-adic representation rho_f attached to f, with O the ring of integers of a finite extension of Q_p, such that rho-bar is isomorphic to the reduction of rho modulo the maximal ideal of O. The weight is Serre's k(rho-bar) and the level is N(rho-bar) = 1; conductor one does not assert that the p-adic lift is unramified at p.
hypotheses: p is odd throughout the proof; the cases p = 2 and p = 3 of the level-one statement are due to Tate and to Serre respectively and are cited, not reproved
the theorem is for GL_2 over Q; no analogue for other base fields or higher rank is claimed
the embedding iota_p: Qbar -> Qbar_p is fixed in advance and the statement is relative to it

the modularity lifting inputs used are restricted: either the p-adic lift is crystalline at p of weight k <= p+1 (ordinary when the weight is p+1), or it is of Hodge-Tate weights (1,0) and Barsotti-Tate over Q_p(mu_p)
proofSteps: Khare uses the inductive method proposed in Theorem 5.1 of the joint Annals paper, and adds a new 'weight reduction' technique that changes the inductive step.

He uses the results of the Annals paper for weights 2, 4, 6, and after that proves the level-one case without further appeal to classification results for abelian varieties; the only such input that remains is the nonexistence of a semistable abelian variety over Q with good reduction outside 5 (Fontaine, Schoof, Brumer-Kramer).

Taylor's potential modularity and Bockle's deformation-theoretic appendix result are used to construct the minimal and non-minimal lifts; Dieulefait's and Wintenberger's arguments refine them into compatible systems.

The residually degenerate cases are handled by Skinner-Wiles, applicable because the lifts to be proved modular are ordinary up to twist; that ordinarity comes from Breuil-Mezard Prop. 6.1.1 and Savitt Thms 6.11, 6.12.
Kisin's potentially Barsotti-Tate theorem is used only when the p-adic lift is locally at p Barsotti-Tate over Q_p(mu_p).
acceptance: Check the p = 2 and p = 3 level-one cases separately against Tate's and Serre's arguments rather than inheriting them from the odd-p induction
Check that the produced newform has weight exactly k(rho-bar) and level exactly 1, and that the isomorphism is with the residual semisimplification for the chosen prime of O

nodes.title: Corollary 1.2 (conductor a prime, weight 2) and the correction of its proof in KW I
nodes.statement: Khare's Corollary 1.2: if rho-bar is an irreducible, odd, 2-dimensional mod p representation of G_Q with k(rho-bar) = 2 and N(rho-bar) = q a prime, and p > 2, then it arises from S_2(Gamma_1(q)). KW I restate this as Corollary 8.1(i) WITHOUT the hypothesis p > 2 ('Note that p = 2 is included'), treating q = 2 by the earlier Annals paper, and explicitly correct the reference given for the proof: 'the reference to 3 of Theorem 5.1 of [24] is not enough as p may not divide q-1'. The corrected argument uses Theorem 5.1(1) to build an almost strictly compatible weight-2 system with unramified Weil-Deligne parameter away from q and with rho_p minimal at q; at a place above q the Weil-Deligne parameter r_q is either semistable with nontrivial monodromy (so rho_q is semistable of weight 2) or unramified after restriction to Q_q(mu_q) (so rho_q is geometric of weight 2, crystalline over Q_q(mu_q)); the level-one theorem gives modularity of rho-bar_q, possibly reducible, and then part (2) of Theorem 6.1 of [24] - Khare's level-one paper in its published Duke numbering, NOT the Annals paper - concludes, with its Skinner-Wiles references [39], [40] augmented by the correction [41]. The semistable case uses [36] = T. Saito, Modular forms and p-adic Hodge theory, and the other case the proof of Theorem 5.1(3 ii) of [24].
hypotheses: rho-bar irreducible and odd with k(rho-bar) = 2 and N(rho-bar) = q prime
Khare's version additionally assumes p > 2; KW I's Corollary 8.1(i) does not, and its proof imports the case q = 2 from [22] = the KW Annals paper
one may assume the projective image of rho-bar is not dihedral; otherwise KW I Lemma 6.2 applies directly

the final step uses (2) of Theorem 6.1 of [24] = Khare, Duke Math. J. 134 (2006); the library copy of [24] is the arXiv v1 preprint, which has no Theorem 5.1 or 6.1 (its compatible-system result is Proposition 3.1), so these corrected references cannot be resolved from the library

Split on the shape of r_q: semistable with nontrivial monodromy, or unramified after restriction to Q_q(mu_q).

nodes.title: Bockle's appendix: presentation of the minimal deformation ring and R_empty = T_empty
nodes.statement: Proposition 1: let rho and a set X of deformation conditions be given, S a finite set of places outside which deformations of type X are unramified. Assume (a) for l in S minus {p, infinity} the local ring R_{X,l} is a complete intersection, flat over Z_p, of relative dimension h^0(G_l, Ad_X(rho)) - Delta_l, and (b) R_{X,p} is a complete intersection, flat over Z_p, of relative dimension h^0(G_p, Ad_X(rho)) + 1 + d - Delta_p. With Delta the sum of the Delta_l, then R_X is isomorphic to O[[x_1,...,x_{n+d}]]/(f_1,...,f_{n+Delta}). Corollary 1: each of R_empty and R_Q^{alpha-new} has a presentation with m <= n relations. Lemma 2: a CNL O-algebra finite over O with a presentation having m <= n relations is a complete intersection, finite flat over O. Corollary 2: if R_Q is finite over O then R_empty is a complete intersection, finite flat over O. Theorem 1: if for some auxiliary set Q of primes one has an isomorphism R_Q -> T_Q of finite flat W(k)-algebras, then the canonical morphism R_empty -> T_empty of minimal rings is an isomorphism as well.
hypotheses: d and Ad_X(rho) are tied to whether X fixes a determinant: d = 0 and Ad_X = Ad^0 if the determinant is fixed, otherwise d = 1 and Ad_X = Ad
Proposition 1's proof uses that rho is ODD, through the formula of [1], Lem. 5.5(ii); oddness is not decorative here
Lemma 2's proof needs O a discrete valuation ring and R finitely generated as an O-module, so that R/(pi) is finite local over k and the ideal has height n+1

Theorem 1's proof needs T_Q and T_empty finite flat over W(k) ('standard fact') and reduced - T_Q by the choice of Q - and uses Carayol [3] (Ann. ENS 1986) to conclude that a newform unramified at the primes of Q has conductor prime to Q

the case where rho restricted to a decomposition group at p is decomposable and flat is NOT covered by the generic computation Delta_p = 0 and is handled by a separate Lemma 1 following Ramakrishna's thesis
proofSteps: Proposition 1: choose an auxiliary set S_aux, present each R_{X,l} with n_l generators, count relations j_l, and use the global-to-local presentation theorem ([1], Thm 5.6) plus the oddness formula to get n + Delta = j.

Corollary 1 follows by verifying hypotheses (a),(b) in the four cases (i)-(iv) listed, citing [1] Thm 2.4, Thm 3.8, Lem. 3.10/Rem. 3.11, and for the Q-new condition the smoothness R_{X,l} = O[[T]], which the appendix says is 'implicitly shown' in [8] = Ramakrishna, Annals 156 (2002); at p, Delta_p = 0 is quoted from Darmon-Diamond-Taylor [5], Sect. 2, except in the decomposable flat case, where Lemma 1 (from Ramakrishna's thesis and Conrad [4], Thm 1.8(ii), Lem. 3.4, sections 4-5) gives R = W(k)[[X_1, X_2]] by a rigid-analytic fibre argument.

Lemma 2: A = O[[x_1,...,x_n]] is regular local of dimension n+1; finiteness of R over O makes R/(pi) a finite local k-algebra, so the ideal (pi, f_1, ..., f_m) has height n+1, which with m <= n forces m = n (the appendix attributes this to 'the Krull intersection theorem'; the step is Krull's height theorem); by Matsumura Thm 17.4 pi, f_1, ..., f_n is a regular sequence, hence R is a complete intersection and pi is a nonzerodivisor on R, so R is flat over O.

Theorem 1: all four rings in the square R_Q -> T_Q, R_empty -> T_empty are finite flat over W(k) by Corollary 2 and the standard finiteness of Hecke algebras, so it suffices to check the bottom map after tensoring with K; T_Q tensor K and T_empty tensor K are products of copies of Kbar indexed by the sets M_Q, M_empty of normalized eigenforms (of level l^delta N(rho-bar) Q, resp. without Q) lifting rho-bar; a form in M_Q minus M_empty obtained from R_empty would be unramified at the places dividing Q, forcing its conductor prime to Q by Carayol [3], a contradiction.

nodes.title: The explicit prime-gap inequalities that make the weight recursion terminate
nodes.statement: For each prime p >= 5 one needs a prime P > p (for instance the next prime after p) together with either (i) an odd prime power divisor l^r exactly dividing P-1 such that P/p <= (2m+1)/(m+1) - (m/(m+1))(1/p) where l^r = 2m+1 with m >= 1, or (ii) 2^r exactly dividing P-1 with r >= 4 such that P/p <= 2^r/(2^{r-1}+2) - ((2^{r-1}-2)/(2^{r-1}+2))(1/p). These are checked by hand for p <= 31; for p > 31 the estimates of Rosser-Schoenfeld give P/p <= 3/2 - 1/30 = 1.46, which suffices because (2m+1)/(m+1) and 2^r/(2^{r-1}+2) are >= 3/2 while m/(m+1) and (2^{r-1}-2)/(2^{r-1}+2) are <= 1 for m >= 1, r >= 4. Consequences used later: (3) p+1 >= ((m+1)/(2m+1))(P-1) + 2 = (P+1) - (m/(2m+1))(P-1), and (4) p+1 >= ((2^{r-1}+2)/2^r)(P-1) + 2 >= (P+1) - (1/2)(P-1). Placement note (reviewer): these are KW I section 7 estimates, consumed by KW I Theorem 3.2 (stage R27.2, whose atlas text asks for 'every prime estimate'); Khare's own level-one estimates (his section 4, Chebyshev) were not read, so the node does not yet cover R26.3's level-one obligation.
hypotheses: the inequalities are needed only for p >= 5; smaller primes are handled by the separate mod 3 and mod 5 arguments
case (ii) requires r >= 4, i.e. 16 | P-1; r = 1, 2, 3 are not covered by (2)
the numerical verification for p <= 31 is by hand and is a finite exceptional check, not a consequence of the asymptotic estimate

proofSteps: Rosser-Schoenfeld's explicit prime estimates bound the ratio of consecutive primes above 31 by 1.46.
The right-hand sides of (1) and (2) are bounded below by 3/2 - 1/p, which exceeds 1.46 for p > 31.

Inequalities (3) and (4) are algebraic rearrangements of (1) and (2) and are what is actually consumed: they bound the interval of admissible twisting exponents i in the inductive step of Theorem 3.2 so that the new Serre weight satisfies k <= p+1.

nodes.title: Corollary 8.1(ii) and the derivation of the induction's starting point (W_1)
nodes.statement: Corollary 8.1(ii): if rho-bar is an irreducible, odd, 2-dimensional mod p representation of G_Q with k(rho-bar) = 2, unramified outside p and one other odd prime q, tamely ramified at q, such that the order of rho-bar(I_q) is a power of an odd prime t > 5, then rho-bar arises from S_2(Gamma_1(q^2)). Theorem 3.3 - the hypothesis (W_r) for r = 1 - follows from this. Thus the starting point of the KW induction is NOT the conductor-one theorem restated: (W_1) concerns locally good-dihedral representations of weight 2 whose odd conductor has at most one prime divisor, and Corollary 8.1(ii) is the statement about representations ramified at exactly one odd prime q with tame image of odd prime-power order t > 5 - i.e. exactly the shape a good dihedral prime produces.
hypotheses: t is an odd prime, t > 5, and t is different from p and from q: t not p because otherwise the first statement applies, and t not q because rho-bar is tamely ramified at q
one may assume the projective image of rho-bar is not dihedral, the A_4 and S_4 cases reducing to level one because t > 5
the conclusion is stated at level q^2 (S_2(Gamma_1(q^2))); the source gives no further explanation of the exponent
the argument uses modularity lifting results of Skinner-Wiles in the residually reducible branch and Wiles/Taylor-Wiles in the residually irreducible branch
proofSteps: Reduce (ii) to (i). Build an almost strictly compatible lift by Theorem 5.1(1): rho_p unramified outside {p, q}, crystalline of weight 2 at p, with |rho_p(I_q)| = |rho-bar_p(I_q)|.

Consider the mod t reduction rho-bar_t. If it is reducible, or unramified at q (which forces reducibility by the level-one weight-2 case), apply Skinner-Wiles to conclude rho_t is modular; note rho_t is crystalline of weight 2 because the system is almost strictly compatible of weight 2 and t is not 2.

If rho-bar_t is irreducible and ramified at q, then k(rho-bar_t) = 2 by almost strict compatibility and part (i) gives modularity (the ramification at q is unipotent); Wiles/Taylor-Wiles then gives modularity of rho_t.
In the last case, irreducibility of rho-bar_t restricted to Q(mu_t) is checked either from |rho-bar_t(I_q)| = t or from k(rho-bar_t) = 2 together with Lemma 6.2(ii).
acceptance: Check that the produced form has level q^2 and not q, and that this is what (W_1) consumes
Check that the branch where rho-bar_t becomes reducible after the change of prime is actually reachable, so that it is a branch of the proof and not an impossible case

nodes.title: Definition 2.1: good dihedral prime
nodes.statement: Let Q: N -> N be defined by Q(1) = 1 and, for n >= 2, Q(n) = the largest prime dividing n. For rho-bar: G_Q -> GL_2(F_p-bar) continuous, a prime q different from p is a good dihedral prime for rho-bar if (i) rho-bar restricted to I_q is of the form diag(psi, psi^q) with psi a NON-TRIVIAL character of I_q whose order is a power of an odd prime t such that t divides q+1 and t > max(Q(N(rho-bar)/q^2), 5, p); and (ii) q is 1 mod 8, and 1 mod r for every prime r with r <= max(Q(N(rho-bar)/q^2), p). If such a q exists, rho-bar is called locally good-dihedral (for the prime q), or q-dihedral.
hypotheses: psi must be nontrivial and of order a power of an ODD prime t with t | q+1 - so psi is of level 2 at q and t does not divide q-1
the bound on t is taken against Q(N(rho-bar)/q^2), i.e. the largest prime dividing the prime-to-q part of the conductor, together with 5 and p

condition (ii) (q = 1 mod 8 and q = 1 mod r for the primes r in range) is used in the proof of Lemma 6.3(i) to show that q splits or ramifies in any quadratic field K unramified outside the primes at which rho-bar ramifies, both of which are then excluded
the definition is a property of the pair (rho-bar, q), and both conditions refer to N(rho-bar), so it is not stable under arbitrary changes of level
proofSteps: The definition is stated outright in the source. Its purpose, made explicit in Remark 2 after the proof of Theorem 3.2, is that starting with a q-dihedral rho-bar in characteristic P ramified at a set S, the proofs of Theorems 3.1 and 3.2 only need residual representations in characteristic at most max over l in S minus {q} of (P, l) - which is exactly the range in which (i) and (ii) have been imposed.

nodes.title: Lemma 6.3: a locally good-dihedral representation has non-solvable, non-A_5 image, and the property propagates through a compatible system
nodes.statement: Let rho-bar be locally good-dihedral for a prime q. (i) The image of rho-bar is not solvable and its projective image is not isomorphic to A_5. (ii) Let (rho_iota) be any compatible system lifting rho-bar whose ramified primes are contained in the prime divisors of N(rho-bar)p, and such that rho_p restricted to D_q is a minimal lift of rho-bar restricted to D_q. Then for any prime r <= max(Q(N(rho-bar)/q^2), p), any mod r representation rho-bar_r arising from (rho_iota) is again locally good-dihedral for the prime q, and hence has non-solvable image with projective image not A_5.
hypotheses: in (ii) the two hypotheses on the system are essential: the ramification set must be contained in the primes dividing N(rho-bar)p, and rho_p must be MINIMAL at q
the range of r is bounded by max(Q(N(rho-bar)/q^2), p), exactly the bound built into Definition 2.1
the argument for (i) uses t > 5 twice: to exclude A_5, and to force the projective image to be dihedral in the solvable case via Dickson
proofSteps: (ii) follows from compatibility, (i), and two observations: for t different from 2 and r a prime different from t, the reduction map is bijective on a dihedral subgroup D_{2t^a} of PGL_2(Q_r-bar) sitting inside PGL_2(O); and for r <= max(Q(N(rho-bar)/q^2), p) one has max(Q(N(rho-bar_r)/q^2), r) <= max(Q(N(rho-bar)/q^2), p).
(i): since t divides q+1 and not q-1, rho-bar restricted to D_q is irreducible, hence so is rho-bar; since t > 5 the projective image cannot be A_5.

If the image were solvable then by Dickson the projective image is dihedral, so rho-bar is induced from a quadratic K unramified outside the primes ramified in rho-bar; the primes s different from q at which rho-bar is ramified satisfy q = 1 mod s (and 1 mod 8 if s = 2), so q either splits or ramifies in K. Splitting contradicts irreducibility of rho-bar restricted to D_q; ramification contradicts t being odd.

nodes.title: Dickson's classification, its p = 2 refinement, and the dihedral and degenerate weight lemmas
nodes.statement: Dickson: for any prime p, a finite subgroup of GL_2(F_p-bar) acting irreducibly on the plane has projective image isomorphic to a dihedral group, A_4, S_4, A_5, PSL_2(F_0) or PGL_2(F_0) for F_0 a finite subfield of F_p-bar; PSL_2(F_0) is simple nonabelian as soon as |F_0| >= 4. Lemma 6.1: a finite SOLVABLE subgroup G of GL_2(F_2-bar) acting irreducibly has dihedral projective image. Lemma 6.2(i): an S-type rho-bar with dihedral projective image is modular, and arises from S_{k(rho-bar)}(Gamma_1(N(rho-bar))). Lemma 6.2(ii): if rho-bar is of S-type, p >= 3, 2 <= k(rho-bar) <= p+1, and rho-bar restricted to G_{Q(mu_p)} is reducible, then k(rho-bar) is (p+1)/2 or (p+3)/2.
hypotheses: Lemma 6.1 is over F_2-bar and uses that an element of GL_2(F_2-bar) of 2-power order has order 1 or 2, and that a Sylow 2-subgroup is unipotent

Lemma 6.2(i) at p = 2 is not 'well known': it goes through the method of Proposition 10 of Serre's Duke paper (the 'trick of Serre'), with the refined level and weight coming from a separate theorem of Wiese
Lemma 6.2(ii) needs p > 2 (the projectivisation must be tamely ramified at p) and the normalized weight range 2 <= k <= p+1
proofSteps: Lemma 6.1: by Dickson the projective image is dihedral, A_4 or S_4; S_4 is excluded because 2-power-order elements of GL_2(F_2-bar) have order at most 2; A_4 is excluded because it has a normal subgroup of order 4, which forces G into the upper triangular matrices, contradicting irreducibility.

Lemma 6.2(ii): for p > 2 the projectivisation is tamely ramified at p so its inertia image is cyclic; as the quadratic subfield of Q(mu_p) is ramified at p, that image has order 2, and the two possible weights follow from Serre's definition of k.
acceptance: Check Lemma 6.2(ii) against Serre's weight recipe directly, recovering (p+1)/2 and (p+3)/2 from the level-1 and level-2 tame cases
Check that Lemma 6.1 fails over F_p-bar for odd p, by exhibiting a solvable irreducible subgroup with projective image A_4

nodes.statement: For an integer r >= 1: (L_r) all rho-bar of S-type are modular provided (a) rho-bar is locally good-dihedral, (b) k(rho-bar) = 2 IF p = 2, and (c) N(rho-bar) is odd and divisible by at most r primes. For an integer r >= 0: (D_r) all rho-bar of S-type are modular provided (a) rho-bar is locally good-dihedral, (b) the residue characteristic of rho-bar is an odd prime, and (c) N(rho-bar) is NOT divisible by 2^{r+1}. nodes.title: Theorem 3.2 (reduction to weight 2): (W_r) implies (L_r), with its three-part proof
nodes.statement: For a positive integer r, (W_r) implies (L_r). The proof is an induction on the residue characteristic p, with the cases p = 3 and p = 5 done separately and a general inductive step. Mod 3: lift a q-dihedral rho-bar with k(rho-bar) <= 4 by Theorem 5.1(2), pass to rho_2; rho-bar_2 is q-dihedral hence non-solvable, k(rho-bar_2) = 2 by almost strict compatibility, and N(rho-bar_2) has at most r+1 prime divisors, namely those of N(rho-bar) together with 3. If rho-bar_2 is unramified at 3 one concludes by (W_r) and Theorem 4.1. Otherwise rho-bar_2 restricted to I_3 is nontrivial unipotent (because omega_3 has order 2), so rho-bar_2 restricted to D_3 is, up to unramified twist, upper triangular with diagonal (chi_2, 1); apply Theorem 5.1(4) with chi' = omega_{3,2}^2 and conclude through rho-bar'_3. Mod 5: same with chi' = omega_5^2 in Theorem 5.1(3), producing rho-bar'_5 of weight 4, then splitting on whether 3 divides N(rho-bar'_5). Inductive step: let P be the next prime after p, choose a prime power l^r exactly dividing P-1 satisfying (1) or (2) of section 7, and choose the twisting exponent i in the interval [(2m+1)^{-1} m (P-1), (m+1)(2m+1)^{-1}(P-1)] (respectively an even i in [(P-1)/2, (2^{r-1}+2)/2^r (P-1)] when l = 2); the estimates (3) and (4) then give k(rho-bar'_P) <= p+1 after a twist.
hypotheses: throughout, rho-bar is locally good-dihedral, p is odd, N(rho-bar) is odd and has at most r prime divisors
the mod 3 step uses that omega_3 has order 2, so ramification at 3 is unipotent; the mod 5 step uses that omega_5 has order 4
the choice of i in the inductive step is constrained by the prime estimates AND, when l = 2, by a parity condition needed for the lift to be odd
at every change of prime the new residual representation is again q-dihedral by Lemma 6.3, which is what keeps the residually degenerate cases out of reach
proofSteps: Base cases p = 3 and p = 5 are run explicitly, each splitting on whether the auxiliary residual representation is ramified at the old prime.

In the general step, Theorem 5.1(2) gives a weight-2 lift with prescribed inertial Weil-Deligne parameter at P; reduction mod l gives rho-bar_l, q-dihedral with conductor divisible by at most r+1 primes.
If rho-bar_l is unramified at P the conductor drops to r primes and the inductive hypothesis (in characteristic l <= p) applies.

Otherwise Theorem 5.1(3) is applied to a twist rho-bar'_l with 2 <= k <= l+1 (when l is odd), producing a system whose P-adic member has residual weight <= p+1 by the estimates, and whose conductor is odd with at most r prime divisors.
Modularity is then transported back along the two systems, which are linked at l, by two applications of Theorem 4.1.

It remains to show rho-bar'_P modular (and, at p = 5, rho-bar'_5): split on whether p (resp. 3) divides N(rho-bar'_P). If it does, lift by Theorem 5.1(2) and reduce mod p, obtaining an odd conductor with at most r prime divisors (a subset of those of the prime-to-p part of P N(rho-bar'_P)); if it does not, lift by Theorem 5.1(1) and reduce mod p. In both cases the residual representation is q-dihedral and modular by the inductive hypothesis (at p = 5, by the mod 3 case), and Theorem 4.1 gives modularity of the lift, hence of rho-bar'_P.

nodes.title: Theorem 3.1 (killing ramification in weight 2): (L_r) implies (W_{r+1})
nodes.statement: For a positive integer r, (L_r) implies (W_{r+1}). Proof: let rho-bar be of S-type, locally good-dihedral for a prime q, with k(rho-bar) = 2 and N(rho-bar) odd divisible by at most r+1 primes. Choose a prime s different from q dividing N(rho-bar). By Theorem 5.1(1) construct an almost strictly compatible lift (rho_iota) and consider rho_s. Then rho-bar_s is of S-type, is q-dihedral and hence has non-solvable image by Lemma 6.3(ii), and N(rho-bar_s) is divisible by at most r primes, because the prime divisors of N(rho-bar_s) form a subset of the prime divisors of the prime-to-s part of N(rho-bar). By (L_r) rho-bar_s is modular, and Theorem 4.1 finishes.
hypotheses: s must be different from q: the good-dihedral prime is deliberately not killed at this step
the conductor bookkeeping uses that the ramification at s is absorbed into the coefficient prime, so s drops out of the conductor - this is the whole content of 'killing ramification'
Theorem 5.1(1) requires k(rho-bar) = 2 when p = 2 and gives a lift minimally ramified away from p and crystalline of weight k(rho-bar) at p

Theorem 4.1 requires rho-bar_s to have non-solvable image if s = 2, and rho-bar_s restricted to Q(mu_s) absolutely irreducible if s > 2; the source derives non-solvable image from q-dihedrality via Lemma 6.3(ii), and absolute irreducibility over Q(mu_s) is left implicit (a reducible restriction would make the image solvable)
proofSteps: The proof is three sentences in the source and is reproduced above. The published Annals paper describes the same device in general form in 6.2 ('killing ramification'): given a compatible system (rho_lambda), take lambda_0 above a prime of ramification, apply its Theorem 4.2 to a cyclotomic twist of rho-bar_{lambda_0} to get a system with a strictly smaller ramification set, and induct; its Theorem 6.2 is CONDITIONAL - it assumes the modularity lifting conjecture (MLC), Theorem 3.3 also for k(rho-bar) = p, and de Rham members of weight k(rho-bar) - and concludes only for p > 2 and N(rho-bar) odd.

nodes.title: Theorem 3.4 (raising levels) and Lemma 8.2, with its rationality correction
nodes.statement: Theorem 3.4: assume (D_r) for a given r >= 0. Then any rho-bar of S-type of residue characteristic p with conductor not divisible by 2^{r+1}, and with k(rho-bar) = 2 if p = 2 and r = 0, is modular. The proof passes to an auxiliary prime p_0 > 5, congruent to 1 mod 4, larger than all primes in S union {p}, splitting completely in E, with rho-bar_{p_0} of non-solvable image; such p_0 exists because for p_0 outside S union {p} with p_0 > 5 one has k(rho-bar_{p_0}) = 2 by almost strict compatibility, so the projective image of rho-bar_{p_0}(I_{p_0}) contains an element of order at least 6 and Dickson forces a solvable projective image to be dihedral - a case handled by Lemma 6.2 and the modularity lifting theorem of [12] (Diamond, An extension of Wiles' results, 'Th. 4.1'); moreover for such p_0, rho-bar_{p_0} cannot be induced from the quadratic subfield of Q(mu_{p_0}) by Lemma 6.2(ii). Lemma 8.2: for p congruent to 1 mod 4 and rho-bar: G_Q -> GL_2(F_p) of S-type with non-solvable image, there is a positive-density set of primes q unramified in rho-bar with (i) rho-bar_proj(Frob_q) and rho-bar_proj(c) conjugate in rho-bar_proj(G_Q), (ii) q congruent to 1 modulo every prime <= p-1 and 1 mod 8, (iii) q congruent to -1 mod p. Theorem 5.1(4) then makes q a good dihedral prime for a new system.
hypotheses: Lemma 8.2 is stated for rho-bar valued in GL_2(F_p), NOT GL_2(F_p-bar): the source records that an earlier version allowed F_p-bar and that Dieulefait and Wiese pointed out that a rationality hypothesis may be necessary
p congruent to 1 mod 4 is used to place rho-bar_proj(c) inside PSL_2(F_p) when the projective image is PGL_2(F_p), and to make -1 a square mod p for condition (iii)
the compatibility of the four Chebotarev conditions rests on the intersection L of the field cut out by rho-bar_proj with the relevant cyclotomic field having degree 1 or 2 over Q
condition (ii)'s '1 mod 8' and '1 mod every prime <= p-1', with p = p_0, give Definition 2.1(ii) for the new system in the characteristic s < p_0 used next
proofSteps: Reduce to rho-bar restricted to Q(mu_p) absolutely irreducible (Lemma 6.2) and to non-solvable image at p = 2 (Lemma 6.1).
Build an almost strictly compatible system by Theorem 5.1(2) and discard the finitely many residual representations that are not absolutely irreducible.
Choose the auxiliary prime p_0 as above; apply Lemma 8.2 to rho-bar_{p_0} to get q; apply Theorem 5.1(4) to attach a level-2 character chi' of I_q of p_0-power order, making q good dihedral.
Let s be the largest prime < p_0; rho-bar'_s is good-dihedral for q, s > 2, and N(rho-bar'_s) is not divisible by 2^{r+1}, so (D_r) applies.
Theorem 4.1 transports modularity to (rho'_lambda), then along the link at rho-bar_{p_0} back to (rho_lambda) and rho-bar.

nodes.title: Hypothesis (H), Theorem 9.1, and the ad hoc dyadic weight computation
nodes.statement: Hypothesis (H): let rho: G_Q -> GL_2(O) be continuous, odd, irreducible and p-adic with (i) rho-bar of non-solvable image and modular, and (ii) rho unramified outside a finite set of primes, of weight 2 and potentially crystalline at p; then rho is modular. By Breuil (p different from 2) and Kisin, a crystalline representation of G_K with Hodge-Tate weights 0 and 1 comes from a p-divisible group, so the condition at p may be replaced by 'potentially Barsotti-Tate'. Theorem 9.1: assuming (H), Serre's conjecture is true. The proof first gets (D_1) and characteristic 2 by reversing the roles of 2 and 3 relative to the mod 3 case of Theorem 3.2: construct a weight-2 minimal system, look at rho-bar_3; if it is unramified at 2 conclude by Theorem 1.2 and Theorem 4.1; otherwise rho-bar_3(I_2) is unipotent, so rho-bar_3(D_2) is up to unramified twist upper triangular with diagonal (chi_3, 1), and Theorem 5.1(4) with the two 3-adic characters chi', chi'^2 of I_2 of order 3 gives a system whose 2-adic residual representation has k = 2. Then (D_r) for r > 1 follows: one may assume rho-bar(I_2) is not, up to twist, unipotent, and rho-bar_2 is then modular and rho_2 potentially crystalline of weight 2, so (H) applies.
hypotheses: Hypothesis (H) requires the residual representation to have NON-SOLVABLE image and to be modular; it is not a general lifting statement
the weight-2 and potentially crystalline conditions at p are both needed; the Breuil-Kisin remark only reformulates them
the claim k(rho-bar'_2) = 2 in the proof is given by an ad hoc argument because the reference used elsewhere for residual weights (Savitt) does not cover p = 2
Theorem 9.1 proves Serre's conjecture only under (H), and like the rest of KW I it uses Theorems 4.1 and 5.1, whose proofs are in KW II
proofSteps: The dyadic weight claim: if k(rho-bar'_2) were 4 then rho-bar'_2 would be tres ramifiee, so for any finite extension K of Q_2 of ODD ramification index, rho-bar'_2 restricted to G_K could not be finite flat (asserted without reference). But - the source says 'by Theorem 5.1(2)', although the system was built with Theorem 5.1(4) - there is a finite extension K of Q_2 of ramification index 3 (the order of chi') over which rho-bar'_2 restricted to G_K is finite flat, for instance the field cut out by chi' over the unramified quadratic extension of Q_2. Contradiction, so k(rho-bar'_2) = 2.
Having (D_1) and characteristic 2, one deduces (D_r) for r > 1 by taking rho-bar with rho-bar(I_2) not unipotent up to twist, building a weight-2 minimal system, and applying (H) to rho_2.

nodes.title: What the assembled theorem does and does not assert, and the compatible-system corollary
nodes.statement: The assembled theorem - KW I Theorems 1.2 and 9.1 together with Kisin's theorem [28] discharging Hypothesis (H), and with Theorems 4.1 and 5.1 proved in KW II - is Serre's conjecture for two-dimensional, odd, absolutely irreducible mod p representations of G_Q: each such rho-bar arises from a newform of weight k(rho-bar) and level N(rho-bar) with respect to the fixed embedding iota_p. Its export to compatible systems is Theorem 10.1: (i) a two-dimensional REGULAR compatible system that is irreducible and odd arises up to twist from a newform of weight >= 2; (ii) a two-dimensional IRREGULAR compatible system that is irreducible and odd arises up to twist from a newform of weight 1. The proof of (ii) uses a theorem of Sen and Fontaine (for almost all lambda, rho_lambda is unramified at the residue characteristic of lambda) and then the arguments of Gross and Coleman-Voloch on weight-one forms. No statement is made for base fields other than Q or for representations of rank greater than 2.

the conclusion is 'up to twist'; the twist normalizes the Hodge-Tate numbers to (a, 0) with a >= 0

For a = b = 0, Sen and Fontaine give unramifiedness at the residue characteristic for almost all lambda, and then the Gross and Coleman-Voloch results place rho-bar_lambda in S_1(Gamma_1(N)) with N independent of lambda.

nodes.title: The Dieulefait-Pacetti target: weak Serre modularity, with weight restricted to k >= 2 via Deligne-Serre 6.9
nodes.statement: Target: let rho: Gal_Q -> GL_2(F_p-bar) be an odd continuous irreducible Galois representation. Then rho is modular, i.e. there is a modular form f in S_k(Gamma_0(N), eps) with rho isomorphic to rho_{f,p}. Only 'cohomological' forms, i.e. k >= 2, are considered, following Serre's original conjecture; the source justifies this by the congruence of Deligne-Serre section 6.9, which shows that if rho is congruent to a representation coming from a weight-1 form then it is also congruent to one attached to a cohomological form. The paper proves the WEAK conjecture and then cites Edixhoven for the weight refinement and Ribet (and Boston-Lenstra-Ribet) for the level refinement; it does not reprove either.

nodes.title: The four modularity lifting theorems the simplified proof rests on, with their exact hypotheses
nodes.statement: Theorem 1.4 (p odd, residually irreducible): rho: Gal_Q -> GL_2(Qbar_p) continuous, odd, finitely ramified, with rho-bar restricted to Gal_{Q(sqrt(p*))} absolutely irreducible, rho restricted to Gal_{Q_p} de Rham with Hodge-Tate weights {0, k-1}, k > 1, and rho-bar modular; then rho comes from a weight-k form. Theorem 1.6 (residually reducible, p >= 5): rho continuous, irreducible, odd, finitely ramified, de Rham at p with Hodge-Tate weights {0, k-1}, k > 1, and rho-bar semisimplifying to a sum of two characters; then rho comes from a weight-k form. Theorem 1.7 (p = 3, residually reducible): rho: Gal_Q -> GL_2(Qbar_3) continuous, irreducible, odd, finitely ramified, with rho-bar^{ss} = 1 + chi_3, rho restricted to D_3 not the identity, rho restricted to I_3 of the form (*, *; 0, 1) (ordinary), and det(rho) = psi chi_3^{k-1} for some k >= 2; then rho comes from a weight-k form (page image: only the first bullet carries a bar; the application in Paso 6 checks the second condition for the residual representation, so the printed second bullet is probably meant residually).

nodes.title: Theorem 1.9 (existence of prescribed lifts) and the insertion of the good-dihedral prime
nodes.statement: Theorem 1.9: let rho: Gal_Q -> GL_2(F_p-bar) be odd, continuous, with rho restricted to Gal_{Q(zeta_p)} absolutely irreducible, and with non-solvable image when p = 2. Then rho admits a lift rho: Gal_Q -> GL_2(E) with any one of: (1) p = 2 and k(rho) = 2: a minimal crystalline lift with Hodge-Tate weights {0,1}; (2) p = 2 and k(rho) = 4: a lift with Hodge-Tate weights {0,1}, minimally ramified outside 2, inertial Weil-Deligne parameter at 2 equal to (omega_1 + 1, N) with N the nonzero nilpotent (Steinberg); (3) p > 2: a minimal crystalline lift with Hodge-Tate weights {0, k(rho)-1}; (4) p > 2: a lift with Hodge-Tate weights {0,1}, any inertial type tau_l compatible with rho at primes l in Sigma different from p, unramified outside Sigma, crystalline at p if k(rho) = 2 and Steinberg at p if k(rho) = p+1. Paso 2 uses (4) at an auxiliary prime N chosen by Lemma 1.15 to attach to the system a level-2 character of order q from the unramified quadratic extension Q_{N^2}, making N a good-dihedral prime; Lemma 2.1 then guarantees non-solvable residual image at every prime of S_1 union {2,3}.

nodes.title: Paso 4: removing 2 from the level, via a Steinberg type and an order-3 local type at 2
nodes.statement: Lemma 2.3: let (rho_l) be an almost strictly compatible system with Hodge-Tate weights {0,1}, unramified at 3, whose Weil-Deligne representation at 2 is a twist of Steinberg, and with rho-bar_3 of non-solvable image. Then there is another almost strictly compatible system (rho'_l) with the same Hodge-Tate weights and ramification set, whose 3-adic members are congruent to those of the first, and whose Weil-Deligne type at 2 is given by an order-3 character - in particular with trivial monodromy; modularity of one system is equivalent to modularity of the other. Remark 6 explains why: if the residual representation at 2 has Serre weight 4 (the tres ramifiee case) it is flat only over extensions of even ramification index, whereas the type produced by Lemma 2.3 becomes flat over a cubic extension, forcing the new residual weight to be 2.
